subject: BrightLoop renewal — stair-step capacity plan + QBR scheduling
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Aileen Park <aileen@brightloop.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: BrightLoop renewal — stair-step capacity plan + QBR scheduling

Hi Aileen,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — excited to get the renewal process moving. Based on your usage trends and the goals you shared (shorten latency for inference pipelines and support a seasonal peak in Nov–Dec), we sketched a stair-step renewal that increases committed capacity across the first three quarters of the term. High level: 10% uplift month 1, 25% uplift at Q2 anniversary, and optional burst credits for Nov–Dec.

Proposed next steps / asks:
- Confirm stakeholders who should attend the kickoff QBR (see suggested list below).
- Confirm whether BrightLoop prefers an annual term with staircase increases or a 12+3 month step plan.
- Legal/procurement: any deadlines for receiving the executed SOW/PO?

Suggested QBR windows (PT):
- Tue Aug 25 10:00–11:00
- Thu Aug 27 14:00–15:00
Please let us know which works and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Suggested attendees:
- From BrightLoop: Aileen Park (Data Platform), Procurement (legal/ops), and an engineering lead if available
- From Redwood: Alex Martinez (AM), Karthik Iyer (Solutions), Marissa Cole (CS lead)

Attaching a draft SOW and a usage snapshot to seed the capacity conversation. I called out areas where we can compress lead time for estimate commits.

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_v1.2.docx, usage_snapshot_July2026.csv

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

From: Aileen Park <aileen@brightloop.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightLoop renewal — stair-step capacity plan + QBR scheduling

Alex —

Appreciate the clear plan. We like the stair-step idea but would prefer quarterly checkpoints that let us opt up ahead of anticipated spikes (rather than an automatic increase). Can you turn the 10%/25% numbers into a quarterly ladder we can review in the QBR?

For scheduling: Aug 27 14:00 PT works for the team. I’ll cc procurement separately — they need to confirm PO timing.

Attendees I’ll lock in: myself, our Head of ML (TBD), and procurement.

Thanks —
Aileen
Head of Data Platform, BrightLoop
aileen@brightloop.com

From: procurement@brightloop.com

Subject: Re: BrightLoop renewal — stair-step capacity plan + QBR scheduling

Hello Alex,

Procurement here. A few items before we can route to finance/legal:
1) Please provide a clean SOW (finalized) and a short summary of SLAs (latency SLOs and uptime) we can attach to the PO.
2) Our standard review window is 10 business days after receipt of final docs. If Redwood needs an earlier start date, flag that now.
3) Also attach the completed vendor questionnaire — we require SOC2 attestation in the packet.

I’m attaching our intake form and vendor_questionnaire.pdf.

Regards,
BrightLoop Procurement
procurement@brightloop.com

Thanks for the checklist. I’m attaching the updated SOW (Redwood_SOW_v1.2.docx) with the SLA summary included on page 2, and a completed vendor_questionnaire.pdf. We can also surface SOC2 type II report via our secure link if you need it for legal review.

Quick internal note — Alex/Marissa, I can own the capacity sizing in the QBR and bring two runbook options: (A) conservative commit + burst credits; (B) aggressive commit with pre-warmed GPU pool. For their Nov–Dec spike we’ll recommend a phased warm-up to avoid cold-start latency.

I’ll prepare a short slide (2–3 bullets) on each option and a cost delta table before the call.
